statement.p: A stone thrown upward from the top of a 99 ft cliff at 133 ft/s eventually falls to the beach below. (For this problem take the acceleration due to gravity to be g = -32 \ \mathrm{ft/s^2}; take upwards to be a positive direction.)
(a) How long does the stone take to reach its highest point?
(c) How long before the stone hits the beach?
(d) What is the velocity of the stone on impact?

static.solution:
h = -16t^{2}+133t+99.
Taking the first derivative, we get v = -32t+133.
The second derivative is the acceleration due to gravity, a = -32.
(a) At its highest point, the stone's velocity is zero: v = -32t+133 = 0, so that t = 4.15625\ {\rm s}.
(b) At t=4.15625\ {\rm s}, the height is h = -16\cdot 4.15625^{2}+133\cdot 4.15625+99 = 375.391\ {\rm ft}.
(c) When the stone hits the beach, h = 0 = -16t^{2}+133t+99. Solving, we get t = 9 s.
(d) Impact is at t=9. The velocity, v, at this time is v = -32\cdot 9+133 = -155\ {\textstyle\frac{\rm\mathstrut ft}{\rm\mathstrut s}}. The velocity is negative because the stone is falling.
